subject: the team handbook that says how engineers respond to a production incident
conclusion: An incident moves through six steps: detect, triage, escalate if needed, mitigate, resolve and review.
why: A fixed sequence means nobody has to decide what to do next under pressure. Mitigation comes before the root cause, so customers stop losing first.

glossary.definition: the person who coordinates the response and owns the updates
a written review of an incident that looks for causes in systems, not people

flow.title: The life of one incident
flow.text: A staged process with one optional branch: triage leads to escalation when mitigation takes too long.

items.label: Detect
items.desc: An alert, a customer report or an engineer opens the incident and pages on-call.

items.label: Triage
items.desc: The on-call engineer sets a severity within 15 minutes and names a commander for SEV1 and SEV2.

items.label: Escalate
items.desc: Escalation pages the secondary engineer and, for payments or SEV1, the leads.

items.label: Mitigate
items.desc: The team stops the harm first: roll back, fail over or switch the feature off.

items.label: Resolve
items.desc: The commander declares the incident resolved after 30 minutes of normal metrics.

items.label: Review
items.desc: Every SEV1 and SEV2 gets a blameless postmortem within five working days.

facts.text: A page that the primary does not acknowledge in 10 minutes goes to the secondary.
A SEV1 needs a status update every 30 minutes.

inferred: The handbook assumes one incident at a time; it does not say who commands two concurrent SEV1s.

lines.name: open
lines.text: Someone notices a problem and opens the incident.

lines.name: triage
lines.text: On-call sets a severity, and escalates if mitigation takes too long.

lines.name: close
lines.text: The team stops the harm, confirms recovery and writes the review.

lines.name: fast
lines.text: Acknowledge a page in five minutes and set a severity in fifteen.

lines.name: slow
lines.text: Escalate after thirty minutes and review within five working days.
